arxiv-1801-07124.title: DECal, a Python tool for the efficiency calculation of thermal neutron detectors based on thin-film converters Journal: Computer Physics Communications
arxiv-1801-07124.creator: Álvaro Carmona Basáñez, Kalliopi Kanaki, Francesco Piscitelli
arxiv-1801-07124.description: Abstract The Detector Efficiency Calculator (DECal) is a series of Python functions and tools designed to analytically calculate, visualise and optimise the detection efficiency of thermal neutron detectors, which are based on thin-film converters. The implementation presented in this article concerns 10 B-based detectors in particular.

arxiv-2105-11347.title: IITP at AILA 2019: System Report for Artificial Intelligence for Legal Assistance Shared Task
arxiv-2105-11347.creator: Baban Gain, Dibyanayan Bandyopadhyay, Arkadipta De, Tanik Saikh, Asif Ekbal
arxiv-2105-11347.description: Abstract In this article, we present a description of our systems as a part of our participation in the shared task namely Artificial Intelligence for Legal Assistance (AILA 2019) . This is an integral event of Forum for Information Retrieval Evaluation - 2019 .

arxiv-2207-00021.title: Quantum conformal symmetries for spacetimes in superposition
arxiv-2207-00021.creator: Viktoria Kabel, Anne-Catherine de la Hamette, Esteban Castro-Ruiz, Časlav Brukner
arxiv-2207-00021.description: Abstract Without a complete theory of quantum gravity, the question of how quantum fields and quantum particles behave in a superposition of spacetimes seems beyond the reach of theoretical and experimental investigations. Here we use an extension of the quantum reference frame formalism to address this question for the Klein-Gordon field residing on a superposition of conformally equivalent metrics.

arxiv-2305-02239.title: The Benefits of Label-Description Training for Zero-Shot Text Classification
arxiv-2305-02239.creator: Lingyu Gao, Debanjan Ghosh, and Kevin Gimpel
arxiv-2305-02239.description: Abstract Pretrained language models have improved zero-shot text classification by allowing the transfer of semantic knowledge from the training data in order to classify among specific label sets in downstream tasks. We propose a simple way to further improve zero-shot accuracies with minimal effort. We curate small finetuning datasets intended to describe the labels for a task.

arxiv-2308-03857.title: Degrees in random m m -ary hooking networks
arxiv-2308-03857.creator: Kiran R. Bhutani, Ravi Kalpathy, Hosam Mahmoud
arxiv-2308-03857.description: Abstract The theme in this paper is a composition of random graphs and Pólya urns. The random graphs are generated through a small structure called the seed. Via Pólya urns, we study the asymptotic degree structure in a random m m -ary hooking network and identify strong laws.

arxiv-2409-05970.title: Nonholonomic momentum map reduction and a Chaplygin-type foliation
arxiv-2409-05970.creator: Paula Balseiro, Danilo Machado Tereza
arxiv-2409-05970.description: Abstract This paper presents a set-up for momentum map reduction of nonholonomic systems with symmetries, extending previous constructions in [ 3 , 25 ] , based on the existence of certain conserved quantities and making essential use of the nonholonomic momentum bundle map of [ 10 ] .

arxiv-2502-09011.title: Statistical analysis of Multipath Entanglement Purification in Quantum Networks
arxiv-2502-09011.creator: Rajni Bala ∗ , Md Sohel Mondal ∗ , Siddhartha Santra Department of Physics and Center of excellence in Quantum information, computation, science and technology, Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400076, India ∗ Equal contribution
arxiv-2502-09011.description: Abstract In quantum networks, a set of entangled states distributed over multiple, alternative, distinct paths between a pair of source-destination nodes can be purified to obtain a higher fidelity entangled state between the nodes. This multipath entanglement purification (MP-EP) strategy can exploit the network’s complex structure to strengthen the entanglement connection between node pairs separated by appropriate graph distances.

arxiv-2510-04376.title: Categorical Invariants of Learning Dynamics
arxiv-2510-04376.creator: Abdulrahman Tamim
arxiv-2510-04376.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Abdulrahman Tamim. Neural network training is typically viewed as gradient descent on a loss surface. We propose a fundamentally different perspective: learning is a structure-preserving transformation (a functor) between the space of network parameters and the space of learned representations. This categorical framework reveals that different training runs producing similar test performance often belong to the same homotopy class (continuous deformation family) of optimization paths.

pmc-10542731.description: A pararectal mass’ specific diagnosis can be challenging as a broad range of both benign and malignant tumors are possible. Many of these lesions are congenital and do not require treatment, if asymptomatic. Special attention is to be paid when imaging findings are not typical. In such cases, definitive diagnostic can require surgical excision.

pmc-10579896.title: Mindfulness-based stress reduction is linked with an improved Cognitive Reflection Test score
pmc-10579896.creator: Léa Lachaud, Baptiste Jacquet, Maxime Bourlier, Jean Baratgin
pmc-10579896.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Initially, dual-process theories suggested that the existence of two different cognitive systems explained why many participants do not find the correct answer in many reasoning tasks. The Cognitive Reflection Test (CRT) is one such task. It contains three questions with incorrect answers (typically associated with intuition and thus system 1 which processes information automatically) and correct answers (typically associated with deliberate thinking and thus system 2 which involves the conscious processing of information).

pmc-11359149.creator: Laura Seijas-Pereda, David Carmena, Carlos Rescalvo-Casas, Marcos Hernando-Gozalo, Laura Prieto-Pérez, Juan Cuadros-González, Ramón Pérez-Tanoira, Harunor Rashid

pmc-11452541.title: Deciphering autism heterogeneity: a molecular stratification approach in four mouse models
pmc-11452541.creator: Caroline Gora, Ana Dudas, Océane Vaugrente, Lucile Drobecq, Emmanuel Pecnard, Gaëlle Lefort, Lucie P Pellissier
pmc-11452541.description: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental condition characterized by impairments in social interaction and communication, as well as restrained or stereotyped behaviors. The inherent heterogeneity within the autism spectrum poses challenges for developing effective pharmacological treatments targeting core features. Successful clinical trials require the identification of robust markers to enable patient stratification.

pmc-13267699.title: Carrier-free targeted co-assembly of glycyrrhizin and puerarin overcomes ocular barriers for corneal alkali burn therapy via macrophage reprogramming
pmc-13267699.creator: Hanhan Peng, Haoyu Li, Jianing Lin, Licheng Li, Muyan Li, Hai Huang, Junyong Wu, Baihua Chen
pmc-13267699.description: Corneal alkali burns (CAB) represent a devastating form of ocular trauma characterized by the rapid penetration of alkaline agents, triggering a destructive cascade of inflammatory infiltration, neovascularization, and fibrotic remodeling that compromises ocular transparency. Current pharmacological interventions are largely palliative and severely hampered by rapid precorneal clearance and poor epithelial penetrability.

pmc-13675133.title: Leadership Education for Doctors—A Scoping Review
pmc-13675133.creator: Naja Vaaben, Alberte Nielsen, Constance Thyra Giertz Christiansen, Nikoline Svensson, Peter Dieckmann, Ann Merete Møller
pmc-13675133.description: IntroductionClinical leadership is essential for patient safety and effective healthcare delivery.
